Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a prominent, lobulated soft tissue mass in the anterior mediastinum (retrosternal space on lateral view) accompanied by blunting of the costophrenic angles bilaterally, indicative of pleural effusions. This combination of an anterior mediastinal mass and bilateral pleural effusions is highly suggestive of a malignant process such as thymoma or lymphoma with possible vascular invasion or metastatic spread.
